title: Wastewater surveillance captures multi-marker responses to short-term examination stress in a university population

Thai ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0003-0042-3057 1 Show authors Nature Water ( 2026 ) Cite this article Save article View saved research 8 Altmetric Metrics details Abstract Young people frequently experience academic stress that may affect mental health and coping behaviours, yet population-level monitoring relies on self-reports or prescription data with limited temporal resolution. Here we use wastewater surveillance to assess short-term, multi-system stress dynamics in a university population. Wastewater samples collected in 2022 from an Australian campus (~30,000 people) were analysed for oxidative stress biomarkers, antidepressants, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder medication and behavioural indicators including alcohol, nicotine and tobacco biomarkers, paraxanthine (caffeine biomarker) and acesulfame. Temporal patterns during examination period were compared with teaching periods and a contemporaneous general-population catchment (~120,000 residents). Difference-in-differences analysis showed a marked university-specific increase in 8-hydroxyguanine (8-OHG), weaker evidence for 8-hydroxy-2′-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG) and consistent but non-significant positive antidepressant consumption trends during examination period. Ritalinic acid and amphetamine, total nicotine and tobacco-derived nicotine, and alcohol remained relatively stable, whereas paraxanthine and acesulfame significantly decreased. By integrating multiple biomarkers, wastewater surveillance provides a non-invasive and complementary tool for identifying periods of increased mental health burden and informing timely public health interventions in university populations.
